repo.last-accessed-by-help: Last recorded authenticated user. Anonymous requests do not replace this value.
repo.downloads-30d-help: Successful GET requests recorded in the last 30 days (includes partial responses). Limited to retained audit history and requests to this repository; group requests are excluded.
announce.hint: Shown to every signed-in user on the main page. Leave empty and save to remove the banner.
announce.placeholder: Markdown supported: # heading, **bold**, `code`, lists, links, and :emoji: shortcodes.
announce.title: Announcement
approval.bulk-description: Approve a repository's entire pending queue in one action. Turn on "Approve only Clean packages" to approve just the packages with no known advisories and leave the rest pending.
approval.clean-only-hint: Approve and cache only packages whose scan found no known advisories. Vulnerable and unscanned packages stay pending for individual review.
approval.cvss-help: This is the CVSS version 3.x base score, which ranges from 0 to 10 and is calculated from the advisory's CVSS vector. A higher number means a more severe vulnerability. A score of 9.0 or above is critical, 7.0 or above is high, 4.0 or above is medium, and anything above 0 is low.
approval.deny-version-hint: Blocks one exact version even when the package is approved. Applies immediately, including already-cached copies.
approval.description: Review quarantined package requests across proxy and hosted repositories.
approval.no-approvers: No users currently have approve permission for this repository.
approval.no-queue: No repository currently has pending requests.
approval.not-scanned: Not scanned yet. The scan runs asynchronously after the request is queued; reload in a moment.
approval.queue-description: Quarantine queue for proxied and uploaded packages. Approve or reject requests before artifacts are served.
approval.read-only: You have read-only (auditor) access. Approval actions are disabled.
approval.rule-allow-note: Pre-approves the whole package: the first request is served without waiting in the queue.
approval.rule-block-note: Blocks the whole package, including already-cached content.
approval.rule-block-version-note: Blocks only this exact version; other versions of the package keep flowing.
approval.title: Approvals
approval.version-optional: Version (optional — leave empty to block the whole package)
approval.version-unknown: unknown (metadata request blocked before a version was resolved)
common.invalid-regex: Invalid regular expression. Results keep the last valid search until the pattern is fixed.
common.name: Name
common.name-rule: Letters, digits, dash and underscore only.
common.no-search-matches: No rows match the current search.
common.search-all-columns: Search all columns, wrap /pattern/ for regex
coverage.alarm-hint: After each scheduled scan, the projects still to migrate are posted to the receivers selected here.
coverage.alarm-preview-sample: No scan has completed yet, so this preview uses example numbers.
coverage.ci-hint: Whether the project's CI pipeline runs its build through forklift.
coverage.cron-hint: Five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week. For example 0 10 * * 1-5 is weekdays at 10:00.
coverage.description: How much of the organisation's source actually builds through forklift, measured by scanning each GitLab project's CI and package-manager configuration.
coverage.disabled: Coverage scanning is turned off. Set coverage.gitlab.enabled to true in the chart, or FORKLIFT_COVERAGE_ENABLED=true, to turn it on.
coverage.exclude-topics-hint: Comma separated GitLab topics. A repository carrying one opts itself out without a change here.
coverage.fill-required: Fill in the required fields before saving.
coverage.forklift-host-hint: The external domain a project's configuration must reference to count as wired. Defaults to the server's external URL, so most deployments leave it empty.
coverage.gitlab-missing: No GitLab instance is configured, so nothing can be scanned. Set FORKLIFT_COVERAGE_GITLAB_URL and FORKLIFT_COVERAGE_GITLAB_TOKEN.
coverage.gitlab-unreachable: The GitLab connection is not working
coverage.host-defaulted: Empty uses the server's own external URL.
coverage.host-missing: The forklift host is not set and the server has no external URL, so no project can match. Set one in the coverage settings.
coverage.host-no-dns: DNS did not resolve from forklift. Fine if your builds resolve it elsewhere.
coverage.host-not-bare: enter a bare domain, with no scheme, path or wildcard
coverage.host-not-external: not an external domain, so no build can resolve it
coverage.host-too-long: too long for a host name
coverage.max-branches-hint: How many branches besides the default one are searched for wiring.
coverage.mute-scopes-hint: A muted check is not required for the verdict and is not credited to it. Muting both takes the project out of coverage entirely.
coverage.muted-banner: This project is muted, so nothing below counts towards coverage.
coverage.muted-by-console: Muted from the console; use Unmute to bring it back.
coverage.muted-scopes-banner: These checks are muted, so the verdict below does not ask for them.
coverage.no-groups: No groups yet. Run a scan to see the breakdown.
coverage.no-pipeline-files: No GitLab CI files on this ref.
coverage.not-in-last-scan: The last scan produced no verdict for this project, either because it was excluded at the time or because it was created since.
coverage.project-not-found: That project could not be found.
coverage.receiver-hint: The report is posted to this receiver's webhook. Leave it empty and no report is sent.
coverage.registry-hint: Whether the project pulls its dependencies and base images from forklift.
coverage.scope-hint: What counts as forklift, and how far into each project the scan looks. Which projects are visible at all is decided by the GitLab access token.
coverage.send-report: Send a report after each scheduled scan
coverage.settings-description: What gets scanned, when, and where the report is sent. The GitLab connection itself comes from the environment.
coverage.since-days-hint: Branches with no commit in this window are not searched.
coverage.skip-when-full: Skip the report at full coverage
coverage.skip-when-full-hint: A report nobody has to act on is noise. A manual send still goes out.
coverage.timezone-freeform: Not in the list. Any IANA timezone name can be typed here.
coverage.timezone-hint: Pick one, or type any IANA name. The cron expression is read in this zone.
coverage.title: Forklift coverage
coverage.trend-empty: No trend yet. History builds up one point per scan.
coverage.unavailable: Coverage is not available on this forklift.
coverage.use-search-hint: Answers for the default branch in one call, but runs on a much lower rate limit than the ordinary API.
ha.description: Review storage topology, leader election state, and fencing token for the active cluster.
ha.failover-note: Manual failover gracefully steps this leader down so a standby is elected and takes over. The leader releases its lease and traffic moves to the new leader. This pod stays Ready and can be re-elected later. Use it for planned maintenance or to drain this pod. Expect a brief in-flight disruption while traffic moves.
ha.step-down-confirm-message: This leader gracefully releases its lease and a standby is elected. Traffic moves to the new leader. Expect a brief disruption. This pod stays Ready and can be re-elected later.
ha.stepping-down-notice: Stepping down - a standby is taking over. Traffic follows the new leader.
ha.title: HA Status
label.invalid: A label must be a key or key:value of letters, digits, - and _ (max 64 characters).
login.access-note: Access is limited by your assigned role.
login.description: Manage repository policies, approvals, and scoped tokens.
login.title: Sign in to forklift
notification.delete-blocked: Detach this receiver from every repository before deleting it.
notification.delete-confirm: Repositories selecting this receiver will stop notifying it. This cannot be undone.
notification.description: A receiver is a webhook (Slack/Mattermost-compatible) alerted when a package enters a repository's approval queue. Each repository chooses which receivers to notify in its Settings.
notification.empty: No receivers yet. Add one to start sending approval alarms.
notification.linked-repos-hint: Repositories that send approval alarms through this receiver.
notification.subtitle: · alarm channels
notification.title: Notifications
notification.webhook-note: The webhook URL is never shown again after it is saved. Leave it blank when editing to keep the current URL.
notification.webhook-warning: The webhook URL cannot be viewed again after you save it. You can only replace it with a new one. Keep a copy somewhere safe before you save.
oci.no-images: No tagged images yet. Push with docker or helm or oras.
quota.access-tokens-desc: Maximum number of personal access tokens this user can hold.
quota.hard-limit-desc: A fixed limit that cannot be changed.
quota.login-failures-desc: Consecutive failed password logins. The account locks when the hard limit is reached.
quota.login-failures-robot-desc: Robot accounts are token-only and cannot log in interactively so this quota does not apply.
quota.name: Quota name
quota.soft-limit-desc: A default limit that an administrator can adjust.
quota.title: Quotas
repo.acl-behavior-detail: When enabled, only requests from a matching source IP are served; others receive 403. An empty allow list blocks every request.
repo.allow-licenses: Allow licenses (SPDX id, one per line; empty = allow all but denied)
repo.approval-audit: Package approval is in audit mode. Requests are logged but packages are still served.
repo.approval-on: Package approval is on. An admin must approve a package before this proxy serves it.
repo.approvers-subtitle: · users who can approve this repository
repo.artifact-unavailable: Artifact file is missing from storage.
repo.artifact-unavailable-hosted: Downloads and installs of this artifact fail. Publish this version again to restore it, or ask an administrator.
repo.artifact-unavailable-proxy: Requests for this artifact fail. Delete the cached entry so it is fetched from the upstream again.
repo.auto-approve-clean-desc: Admit a package automatically once its vulnerability scan comes back with no advisories. Requires a scanner; vulnerable and not-yet-scanned packages still await review.
repo.basics-description: Choose the protocol and serving mode. The generated endpoint follows this selection.
repo.block-unresolved: Block versions not yet resolved (block action only)
repo.block-unscanned: Block versions not yet scanned (block action only)
repo.bulk-delete-denied: Deleting artifacts needs admin on this repository.
repo.bulk-delete-help: The selected artifacts are removed from this repository. A proxy can re-cache them on the next request; hosted uploads cannot be recovered.
repo.bulk-label-denied: Labelling needs admin on this repository, or having uploaded the artifact.
repo.bulk-label-help: The label is applied to every selected artifact. Artifacts you may not label are skipped and listed afterwards.
repo.bulk-remove-label-none: None of the selected artifacts carry a label.
repo.bulk-row-denied: Not yours to label or delete. Labelling needs admin on this repository, or having uploaded the artifact.
repo.bulk-select-page: Select every artifact on this page
repo.cooldown-label: Block versions newer than a cooldown window
repo.cooldown-note: Use this when newly published packages should cool down before serving.
repo.delete-confirm: This removes the repository and its cached/hosted artifacts. This cannot be undone.
repo.delete-note: Deleting a repository removes its cached/hosted artifacts. This cannot be undone.
repo.delete-seeded-note: This is a predefined repository, seeded when Forklift first started. It is kept so the default repository layout stays intact, and it would be recreated on the next startup if removed. It cannot be deleted by anyone, including administrators.
repo.deny-licenses: Deny licenses (SPDX id, one per line)
repo.description-hint: Optional free text shown in the repository list and detail pages.
repo.force-delete-help: will be removed. Its bytes are already missing from storage, so nothing further is lost, and the version can be published again afterwards. This cannot be undone.
repo.license-gate: Gate packages by their declared license
repo.license-note: Licenses are resolved per version from deps.dev. A denied license, or any license outside a non-empty allow list, triggers the selected action. Matching is case-insensitive.
repo.list-description: Host and proxy artifacts across Maven, npm, Cargo, Go, and PyPI. Configure per-repository caching and supply-chain policies (age cooldown, package approval).
repo.members-note: Select member repositories in lookup order. The first hit wins.
repo.new-description: Register a hosted, proxy, or group repository for package delivery.
repo.no-access-role: No role grants access to this repository. Add a permission on a role (Roles page) whose pattern matches this repository.
repo.no-access-token: No access token reaches this repository.
repo.no-cached-artifacts: No cached artifacts yet. Pull through the endpoint above to populate the cache.
repo.offline-note: This repository is offline: uploads and downloads are refused (503). Its config and artifacts are kept.
repo.online-note: This repository is online and serving the package protocols.
repo.policy-order-desc-2: and audit gates only log and let it continue.
repo.proxy-description: Configure the remote registry and optional supply-chain cooldown.
repo.public-access-note: Making this repository public allows anyone to download its artifacts without signing in. Uploads and deletes still require authentication.
repo.purge-confirm: This removes every cached or hosted artifact in the repository. The repository and its settings stay. A proxy will re-cache on demand; hosted uploads cannot be recovered.
repo.purge-note: Purging removes all cached/hosted artifacts but keeps the repository and its settings. This cannot be undone.
repo.pypi-legacy-zip-help: Disabled by default. ZIP archives still require one safe project-version root and matching PKG-INFO metadata.
repo.quarantine-desc: · alarm a receiver when a package is quarantined
repo.readonly-note: Read-only view. You can review the configuration but not change it.
repo.receivers-note: Selected receivers get a webhook alarm when a package here enters the approval queue. Manage receivers on the Notifications page.
repo.require-approval: Require approval before serving a package
repo.restrict-by-ip: Restrict access by client source IP
repo.security-controls-group-desc: Access control is enforced at the group entry point; artifact policies run on the member that serves the request.
repo.security-controls-hosted-desc: Access control, security scans, version denies, and approval quarantine are enforced for hosted artifacts.
repo.security-controls-proxy-desc: Access and artifact guards are fixed. Automated assessments run in the configured order, and human approval remains final.
repo.stat-all-clean: All scanned artifacts are clean, no advisories.
repo.stat-none-scanned: No artifacts have been scanned yet.
repo.type.group-desc: Combine repositories behind a single read-only URL
repo.type.hosted-desc: Store artifacts uploaded directly by your team
repo.type.proxy-desc: Cache and serve artifacts from an upstream registry
repo.upload-approval-notice: Uploads to this repository are quarantined and only served after a reviewer approves the package.
repo.upload-complete: Upload complete. Security scans have been queued.
repo.upload-description: Choose a file and Forklift derives the repository path for you, validating the coordinate and collision before any bytes are uploaded.
repo.upload-exists: Validation failed: this path already exists.
repo.upload-fields-auto: Derived from the file you chose. Adjust if needed.
repo.upload-pending: Upload complete and quarantined. The artifact will be served after approval.
repo.upstream-auth-desc: Authenticate requests to a private upstream. Public registries do not require this.
repo.upstream-auth-note: Credentials are stored server side and always shown masked. Leave a masked value untouched to keep the stored secret; type a new value to replace it.
repo.version-deny-detail: Explicitly blocked versions are always checked in the Artifact guard stage.
repo.visibility-private-desc: Downloads require a signed-in account or an access token.
repo.visibility-public-desc: Anyone can download artifacts without signing in. Uploads still require authentication.
role.action-admin: Full control of the repository including settings and upstream credentials.
role.action-approve: Approve or reject package approval requests.
role.action-audit: Read audit logs and administrative pages.
role.action-read: Download artifacts and browse the repository.
role.action-security: Edit repository security policies such as approval, vulnerability and license rules.
role.delete-confirm: Users and group mappings holding this role lose its permissions immediately. This cannot be undone.
role.empty: No roles yet. Create one to grant repository access.
role.list-description: Bundle repository permissions (read, write, delete, approve, audit, security, admin) over name patterns. Open a role to map permissions; roles are assigned to users on each user's detail page.
role.managed-note: This role was configured by a Forklift administrator in the declarative RBAC policy so it cannot be edited here. To change its permissions or delete it ask an administrator to update the policy file and restart forklift.
role.new-description: Define a reusable access profile and optional repository permissions.
role.no-users: No users have this role. Assign it from a user's detail page.
role.permissions-description: Add repository patterns and allowed actions. Wildcards are accepted.
search.type-to-search: Type at least 2 characters to search.
settings.appearance-description: Choose a fixed theme or follow your operating system setting.
settings.card-description: These settings apply only to the current browser.
settings.content-width-description: The default content width for the console. Wide uses the available width on table views.
settings.description: Preferences are saved in this browser until account-level settings are available.
settings.language-description: Store the preferred interface language for this browser.
settings.language.en-description: Use English as the preferred UI language.
settings.language.ko-description: Use Korean as the preferred UI language.
settings.title: Settings
storage.consistency-see-statistics: Open the repository Statistics tab for detail
storage.description: Storage backend health and usage at a glance. MinIO backends also show live cluster capacity and drive status.
storage.fs-note: This instance uses the filesystem backend. MinIO cluster metrics are available only with an S3/MinIO object-storage backend.
storage.title: Storage
token.copy-warning: Copy this token now. It will not be shown again.
token.description-placeholder: What this token is used for
token.edit-permissions-note: Add or revoke repository permissions. The token secret stays the same.
token.expiry-note: Tokens expire after at most one year.
token.hard-limit: This limit is fixed and cannot be changed.
token.help-1: Scoped credentials for package clients, limited to chosen repositories and actions within your own permissions. Use a token as the password in your package manager (npm
token.incomplete-note: Complete all required fields before creating a token.
token.limit-reached: Token limit reached. Revoke one to free a slot.
token.name: Token name
token.new-description: Issue a scoped access token with an expiration date and repository permissions.
token.permissions-description: Add repository patterns and allowed token actions.
token.readonly-note: Read-only: only administrators can create or revoke tokens.
token.revoke-confirm-message: Clients using this token will immediately lose access. This cannot be undone.
token.scopes-required: At least one permission is required
token.subtitle: · scoped credentials for package clients

upload.assets-help: Files are renamed to canonical Maven paths. Add classifiers such as sources or javadoc explicitly.
upload.assets-required: Select a file and extension for every asset.
upload.cancelled: The upload was cancelled. Select Upload artifact to start a new attempt.
upload.cargo-file-help: Select the .crate produced by cargo package.
upload.cargo-help: Forklift validates Cargo.toml and the archive root, then atomically appends the sparse-index entry.
upload.choose-file-first: Choose a file to begin. The coordinates are filled in from it automatically.
upload.classifier-invalid: Only letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen are allowed.
upload.coordinates-required: Group ID, Artifact ID, version, and packaging are required.
upload.delete-publication-help: All files owned by this publication will be removed atomically and package metadata will be rebuilt. This cannot be undone.
upload.generate-pom-help: Forklift creates a Maven 4.0.0 POM from these coordinates.
upload.go-help: Forklift validates the GOPROXY ZIP root and module directive, then creates .mod, .info, list, and @latest atomically.
upload.go-mod-help: If omitted, the ZIP go.mod is used or a minimal file is generated.
upload.go-mod-invalid: The optional module metadata file must use the .mod extension.
upload.go-private-help: For private modules, configure GOPRIVATE or GONOSUMDB for this module path.
upload.go-required: Enter a module path and canonical version, then select one module ZIP.
upload.go-zip-help: Every entry must use the exact module@version/ root.
upload.npm-file-help: Select the .tgz produced by npm pack.
upload.npm-help: Forklift reads name and version from package/package.json and atomically updates the packument.
upload.npm-tag-help: Defaults to latest. SemVer-like tags are rejected.
upload.pom-mode-conflict: Disable POM generation when an unclassified .pom asset is supplied.
upload.pom-supplied: An uploaded POM will be validated against these coordinates.
upload.publication-broken: Some files of this version are missing from storage.
upload.pypi-files-help: Select one or more wheels and at most one .tar.gz source distribution for the same release.
upload.pypi-files-required: Select supported .whl or .tar.gz files for one release.
upload.pypi-help: Name and version are read from wheel METADATA or sdist PKG-INFO. Every file must identify the same release.
upload.replace-ack: I understand that every file in this Maven publication will be replaced atomically.
upload.replace-help: Review the conflicting paths. Confirmation requires delete permission and expires after 30 minutes.
upload.title: Upload artifact
upload.yank-help: Cargo keeps the crate bytes and changes only the selected sparse-index entry. Existing lockfiles can still download a yanked version.
user.delete-note: Deleting a user revokes all of their tokens and role assignments. This cannot be undone.
user.delete-self-note: You cannot delete your own account.
user.impersonate-active-note: Stop your current impersonation before starting another one.
user.impersonate-disabled-note: A disabled account cannot be impersonated.
user.impersonate-modal-note: Your session is replaced by one acting as this user until you stop, or for one hour.
user.impersonate-note: Impersonating signs you in as this user with their permissions, so you see Forklift exactly as they do. Your own session is replaced until you stop impersonating, and the reason you give is written to the server log. Actions you take are recorded as this user, with your account noted alongside.
user.impersonate-reason-hint: At least 10 characters. Recorded in the server log with both usernames.
user.impersonate-reason-placeholder: e.g. reproducing the 403 reported on the npm proxy
user.impersonate-robot-note: A robot account cannot be impersonated because it cannot sign in.
user.impersonate-self-note: You are already signed in as this account.
user.initial-password-note: Set an initial password for this local account.
user.list-description: Local and OIDC accounts. Open a user to map roles, reset the password, or disable access. OIDC users appear automatically at first login.
user.locked-note: Locked after too many failed password attempts - unlock it in Account lockout.
user.lockout-note: When enabled, the account is locked after 5 consecutive failed password attempts and must be unlocked by an administrator.
user.lockout-protected-note: The default admin account cannot be locked out.
user.new-description: Create a local account and optionally assign an initial role.
user.no-role-note: A user with no role cannot access repositories until one is assigned.
user.oidc-note: OIDC users are created automatically at first login.
user.protected-note: This is the default administrator account, created when Forklift first started. Its status is locked active so the system always keeps at least one administrator who can sign in and recover access. It cannot be disabled by anyone, including other administrators.
user.robot-password-note: A robot account cannot sign in. It does not use a password. Create the account and then issue a token from its detail page for automation.
user.self-note: You are signed in as this account, so you cannot disable it yourself. This guards against accidentally locking yourself out of Forklift. If this account needs to be disabled, ask another administrator to do it.
user.status-desc-1: account can sign in to Forklift and use its credentials to pull and publish artifacts, while
user.status-desc-2: immediately revokes that access by stopping all sessions and tokens. The account, its tokens and its role assignments are preserved, so disabling is a reversible alternative to deletion that you can undo at any time by re-enabling.
user.type-robot-desc: Token-only account for automation. It cannot sign in.
user.type-user-desc: Signs in with a password or OIDC and can own tokens.
